segments.title: Too early, then too late
sections: Something Must Happen At The Level

cues.text: You know both halves of this. Price comes down to the zone you marked before the session, the band of prices around a level on your list.
The idea is right, the level is right, so you sell the first touch, with a stop, the resting order that takes you out, above it.
Price spikes through, takes the stop, then falls exactly where you said it would, without you.
The next time you wait. Price reaches the zone, turns, and leaves. Twenty points later you cannot stand it and buy at market, filled at whatever price is there.
Now the only stop with structure behind it is too far away to make sense. So you put it closer, inside nothing, and a pullback takes it.
One entry was too early. The other was too late. Both were on time for the loss.
Now, the chain. Every trade in this course traces one line: idea, the reason to look; setup; trigger; construction, the order itself.
The setup says where and what: a named zone, and a read of what price is doing there. The trigger says when.
A trigger is the price event at the level that says enter now: a bar close, or a fill, that you can point to on the chart.
Order flow, the record of orders at each price, can confirm a trigger. It is never the trigger.
Now, the journal field. It takes one of five values: four slugs, a slug being the short name you log a trigger under, and none.
One: pause-n-go.
Two: resting-limit.
Three: ema-pullback.
Four: level-reclaim.
Five: none. Nothing fired at the level before entry. It is data, not a gap.
The example. A pd-low zone, the prior day’s low, from 24,104 to 24,110. Price arrives at 10:06 a.m. and prints 24,109.75.
A sell at that print has a location, a read waiting to happen, and no trigger. The journal says none.
Move that event to mid-range, 40 points from any zone, and it is the mirror leak: a trigger with no location.
The rule: no entry without a named price event at a named zone. Every entry carries its own trigger in the journal, or none.
Getting it wrong is filling in the trigger field in the evening, from memory, with whatever the chart now shows.
The fix: write the slug and its price condition in the note before you arm the order. No line, no order.

cues.text: Pause N Go is the first trigger. It needs two things, in order. A pause, then a go.
The pause: after the first touch of the zone, at least two 1-minute bars in a row hold inside it.
No 1-minute close goes through the far edge, the side of the zone away from where price arrived.
The go: a 1-minute close beyond the pause’s extreme, its highest price for a long, its lowest for a short. You enter on that close, with the stop behind the far edge.
The example, on a composite chart, invented prices. An on-high zone, the overnight high, 21,664 to 21,668. Price is already accepted above it: a 5-minute bar closed beyond.
Price pulls back and touches 21,668, the near edge, the edge price reaches first, at 10:48 a.m.
The 10:49 bar trades entirely inside the zone. So does the 10:50 bar. Neither closes below 21,664. That is the pause, and its high is 21,668.
The 10:51 bar closes at 21,671.25, above that high. That is the go. The entry is on that close.
The stop rests behind the far edge, at 21,662: 9.25 points from the entry, 37 ticks, a tick being a quarter of a point.
Had the 10:50 bar closed at 21,663.50, below the far edge, there would be no pause and no trigger. The zone gave way on a close.
Two bars of nothing happening is the entire pause. The chart is not being slow. It is being specific.
Every part is a closed 1-minute bar, so anyone with the chart can mark it later.
The session block, early, mid or late, goes on every trade, so your record can show whether the trigger behaves the same all day.
The rule: two held 1-minute bars inside the zone, then a 1-minute close beyond the pause’s extreme in the direction of the read. Enter on that close and no sooner.
Getting it wrong is a buy stop, an order that fires when price trades up to it, one tick above the pause high, filled by a bar that later closes back inside the zone.
You paid to avoid waiting for the close, which means you trust the poke more than the bar that has to agree with it.
The fix: beside the zone, write three boxes. Bar 1 held. Bar 2 held. Close beyond the price. The ticket opens after the third box is ticked, at market on that close, stop attached.

segments.title: The resting limit and the 9 EMA pullback

cues.text: Some triggers are a fill, not a close. A resting limit waits inside the zone. When price comes back and fills it, that fill is the trigger.
It counts only after displacement: a push away from the level, in the direction of your read. Your minimum is set once, on your PlayBook page, your own settings page.
The example. A pd-high zone, the prior day’s high, 21,690 to 21,696. Price runs to 21,738.50 in one leg, over 40 points above it. Your minimum is 20: displacement.
The buy limit goes in at 21,696, the stop at 21,688, behind the far edge. The note reads: resting-limit, intended 21,696, the fill the plan names, written first.
A limit placed before the session is blind. Its trigger field says none. It is a lottery ticket that happens to be on a chart.
The rule: a resting limit is a trigger only when placed after displacement, at a price named in the plan, with the stop behind the far edge.
Getting it wrong is limits parked at every zone before the open. The fix: no ticket until the displacement line is in the note, with its size.
Now, the 9 EMA pullback. An EMA, an exponential moving average, weights recent prices more. Here it only times an entry. It is never a level.
It is for continuation only: price resuming the move it was making. Price pulls back to the zone and a bar closes back on the trend side of the average. Enter on that close.
The example. On a pd-vah zone, the prior day’s value area high, 21,650 to 21,655, bars close below the 9 EMA from 10:33 a.m.
At 10:36 one trades into the zone and closes at 21,658.50, above the average at 21,657.75.
That close is the trigger. The stop goes behind the zone’s far edge, at 21,648, not behind the average.
Two lookalikes are not this trigger: a limit on the average, filled on a wick, and a close back above it after a selloff.
The rule: the 9 EMA pullback fires only in a continuation pullback, with price at the zone, on a closed bar back on the trend side of the average.
Getting it wrong is a long on the first close above the 9 EMA after a selloff, logged as ema-pullback. The average has become the signal.
The fix: write that tag only once the location slug and the setup trend-continuation are in the note. Else, none.

segments.title: The level reclaim, and order flow
sections: Order Flow Confirms; It Never Triggers

cues.text: The level reclaim is a trigger. Price trades through the zone of a level on your Module 6 list, then a 5-minute close comes back through the whole zone. Enter on it.
The example, on a composite chart, invented prices: an on-high zone, 21,488 to 21,494. At 10:02 a.m. price trades down through it, to 21,481.25.
The bar ending at 10:05 closes at 21,490.50, inside the zone. Not a close below it, so the invalidation, the price that proves the idea wrong, has not printed.
The bar ending at 10:10 closes at 21,497.25, above 21,494. That close is the reclaim; the entry is on it.
The stop rests two points under the low of the move, at 21,479.25: 18 points, 72 ticks.
Three closes in this course look alike. Only one of them is allowed to buy anything.
The acceptance close in Module 10 is a read.
The reclaim in Module 11 is part of a read.
This one, a 5-minute close at a listed level, is the trigger.
The rule: a level reclaim is a 5-minute close back through the whole zone of a level on your list. VWAP, the volume-weighted average price, and averages are not on it.
Getting it wrong is reclaimed VWAP in the trigger field, or buying a 1-minute poke back above the zone: any line feels like a level when you want a trade.
The fix: level-reclaim needs a slug from the list and the close time in the note. Without both, none.
Now, order flow. The footprint, the chart of orders at each price, can add evidence to a trigger. It cannot stand in for one.
A confirmed entry has two parts: a recorded confirmation, and a price event. Here the confirmation is aggression failing at the level: the pushing side runs out.
Back to the Pause N Go. The three bars falling into the 10:48 a.m. touch carry deltas, delta being buyers minus sellers.
Minus 142.
Minus 88.
Minus 31. The selling is fading: failing-delta.
The confirmation field gets failing-delta. The trigger field gets pause-n-go. The order still waits for the close.
The rule: record each confirmation by name, and have a trigger that fired at the level. A confirmation with no trigger logs as trigger none.
Getting it wrong is filling the confirmation field after the trade, with whatever the replay shows. The fix: fill it before the trigger bar closes, or leave it none.

segments.title: Best Available Fill, and two cases
sections: Worked Cases: A Re-entry, And A Fill That Drifted

cues.text: Everything so far says when. This part is where you actually got in, and how you feel when price leaves without you.
Best Available Fill is the leak where the read and the level are right but the fill drifts from the level, so the stop the structure needs grows.
The journal records the intended price and the actual fill on every trade. The gap between them, in ticks, is the measurement. A-plus, the top of the four grades, needs it within 2 ticks.
The example. The stop belongs to the structure, not to your fill. If the far edge says 21,688, the stop goes at 21,688, filled at 21,696 or at 21,719.
From 21,696 the stop is 32 ticks away.
From 21,719 it is 124. The same 1R, the amount you risk on one trade, buys about a quarter as many contracts.
Missing a trade is free. It only feels expensive.
Case 1, a composite pd-low short. A Pause N Go fires at 10:30 a.m. Intended price 24,102.75, filled at 24,102.50.
Stop 24,112, behind the far edge.
The first trade stops out at 10:34. The invalidation has not printed, so the setup stands. At 10:40 a second Pause N Go fires: a fresh trigger, same setup.
That is a re-entry. It has no count cap. The kill switch, your daily loss limit, is the cap.
Case 2: one replay, three fills. A pd-high long. Limit at 21,696, stop at 21,688. The level, the read and the stop never change. Only the fill does.
Fill A rests at 21,696. Gap zero, stop 32 ticks, trigger resting-limit.
Fill B chases to 21,719. Gap 92 ticks, stop 124, trigger none. The 2 to 1 check, target at least twice the stop, refuses it.
Fill C chases too, then pulls the stop in to 21,711, above the zone, nothing behind it. The grade is C: the stop check failed.
Only the fill moved, and the fill decided what the trade was: a plan, a trade the plan forbids, or a C.
The rule: write the intended price before every order. Enter only at the zone, on a trigger. Measure the gap on every trade.
Getting it wrong is a market buy 20 points above the zone because it is going without me, then a stop moved up to keep the size. Missing it hurt more than a bad trade.
The fix: no market order while price is outside the zone.

segments.title: Score it, then the assignment
sections: Which Trigger Did You Actually Have?

cues.text: Take your last ten trades. Score each one a point for each of six lines that is true.
One, event. The trigger field holds a slug, and you can point to the bar or the fill.
Two, place. Price was at a named zone from your Module 6 list when it fired.
Three, order. A close-based trigger was entered on the closed bar; a limit went in after the displacement line.
Four, confirmation. The field shows none, or each confirmation by name, filled before the trigger bar closed.
Five, fill. The intended price was written before the order, and the fill landed within 2 ticks.
Six, re-entry. A second entry at the same setup had its own fresh trigger, and the invalidation had not printed.
Lines one and two override the score. Miss line one, no trigger. Miss line two, a trigger without a location.
Six out of six is not a trophy. It is the job description.
Now, reading it. If two or more of ten miss line one or two, nothing else matters yet. For ten trades, the trigger line goes in the note first.
If three or more miss line five, Best Available Fill is your leak.
Otherwise, write the line most missed on your pre-market sheet, the plan written before the open.
Getting it wrong is scoring the ten from memory. The six lines are read off the journal, the field, the note, the fill, never off recall.
Your assignment. Next session, before each order, write one line: the trigger slug and the intended price.
For example: pause-n-go, intended 24,102.75. After the fill, write the gap in ticks beside it. That is the whole assignment.
In one line: the level asks, the trigger is the market’s reply, a closed bar or a fill you can point to, and order flow can only add a note.
No reply, no entry. The stop belongs to the structure, so a drifting fill changes everything except the stop.
Where it goes next. Module 14, Trade Construction, takes a trigger and turns it into an order.
The stop behind the far edge, the 2 to 1 check to a target that is a level, the size from the grade.
In the journal, Module 18, every trade carries the trigger slug or none, the confirmation, the intended price, the fill.
Module 22 turns a trigger into an entry in your own register, the list of ideas you are testing.

check.q: Which two lines override the score?
check.why: A trade that misses line one had no trigger. One that misses line two was a trigger without a location.

check.q: Two or more of your ten trades miss line one or two. For the next ten trades, what goes in the note before the ticket is armed?
check.why: The trigger slug and its price condition go in the note first, until the misses stop.

check.q: Three or more of your ten trades miss line five. Your leak is…
check.why: Line five is the fill. The fill-gap list goes on your weekly review.

check.q: You score the ten from memory, without the journal open. That shows…
options: The score is the same either way
A story: the six lines are read off the journal, never off recall
Recall is enough for ten trades
Only line five needs the journal
check.why: Every line is read off the journal: the trigger field, the note, the intended price and the fill. Memory scores the trades you remember best.

options: The price event at the level that tells you to enter now
questions.why: The setup says where and what. The trigger says when, and order flow can only confirm it.

questions.q: The Pause N Go pause is…
options: At least two 1-minute bars inside the zone with no close through the far edge
questions.why: Then a 1-minute close beyond the pause's extreme is the go.

questions.q: A resting limit is a trigger only when…
options: It was placed after displacement, at a price named in the plan
It is placed before the session
It fills on a touch in a simulator
questions.why: A limit placed before displacement is blind, and its trigger field says none.

options: In the middle of the range
On a wick through the average
In a continuation pullback, with price at the zone, on a closed bar back on the trend side
questions.why: The average times the entry; it is never a level.

options: A 5-minute close back through the whole zone of a level on your list
A wick back into the zone
questions.why: Anything not on the level list, such as VWAP or an average, is trigger none.

questions.q: Order flow, in a trigger, is…
options: The trigger when delta is strong
A confirmation recorded by name, beside a trigger that fired
questions.why: A confirmation with no trigger is logged with trigger none.

questions.q: You are filled 23 points above the zone. The structure says the stop goes at the far edge. Where does the stop go?
options: Pulled in, to keep the size
At the far edge, wherever you were filled
questions.why: The stop belongs to the structure. A wider stop means a smaller size, and a pulled-in stop sits above the zone with nothing behind it.

questions.q: A second entry at the same setup, after the first trade closed, needs…
options: A fresh trigger, with the invalidation not printed
questions.why: A re-entry is the same setup plus a fresh trigger. The kill switch is the only cap.
